body: This looks like a valid issue but a workaround should be to set all other properties before setting the space; setting the body's space is what actually adds the body to the physics simulation, so it's more optimal to set it up completely before doing so.

The issue here is that when setting a transform on a kinematic object, the transform is cached:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3defc856b0f1c727b4346e60615b2b2451916837/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_body_3d.cpp#L562-L563

and then the object is moved using velocities to the new location in the next physics step:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3defc856b0f1c727b4346e60615b2b2451916837/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_body_3d.cpp#L208-L218

If there's a dynamic object at (0, 0, 0), the position where the kinematic object starts before it moves to (100, 100, 100), it will get pushed away by the kinematic object. I think this is a bigger bug.

Godot physics will also set velocities to reach the intended target, but it has a special condition that directly sets the transform if it's the first call to set transform after the body has been made kinematic:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3defc856b0f1c727b4346e60615b2b2451916837/modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_body_3d.cpp#L356-L363

We probably want the same for the jolt module.

Next to this, we probably should return `kinematic_transform` for kinematic objects when calling `PhysicsDirectBodyState3D::get_transform`. Unfortunately this function is currently implemented in the base class, so doesn't have access to that member:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3defc856b0f1c727b4346e60615b2b2451916837/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_shaped_object_3d.cpp#L208-L214

cc @mihe, I'm hesitant to make any changes myself here.

Sorry for taking so long to reply. I've gone back and forth on what to do here, because I frankly find the `first_time_kinematic` stuff in Godot Physics to be a bit of a hack that I've tried to avoid replicating in the Jolt integration.

The fundamental problem here is of course that Godot doesn't differentiate between moving a kinematic body (i.e. integrating a velocity) and teleporting it, which means we're forced to assume that a transform change always means the former. Godot Physics then also has this special case (`first_time_kinematic`) where the very first[^1] transform change is always considered a teleport instead.

However, I want to highlight one important part of all this, which is that the repro shown here does not utilize the `PhysicsServer3D` API in the same way as what the regular physics nodes do. The regular physics nodes (i.e. the ones derived from `CollisionObject3D`) always set the transform _before_ assigning a physics space to the body.

So if you change the order of these:

```gdscript
PhysicsServer3D.body_set_space(body_rid_kinematic, physics_space)
PhysicsServer3D.body_set_mode(body_rid_kinematic, PhysicsServer3D.BODY_MODE_KINEMATIC)
PhysicsServer3D.body_set_state(body_rid_kinematic, PhysicsServer3D.BODY_STATE_TRANSFORM, transform)
```

... to instead be this:

```gdscript
PhysicsServer3D.body_set_mode(body_rid_kinematic, PhysicsServer3D.BODY_MODE_KINEMATIC)
PhysicsServer3D.body_set_state(body_rid_kinematic, PhysicsServer3D.BODY_STATE_TRANSFORM, transform)
PhysicsServer3D.body_set_space(body_rid_kinematic, physics_space)
```

... you'll find that everything works as expected.

With this "correct" ordering the `first_time_kinematic` stuff becomes more of a bug than anything else in my opinion, since your very first transform change (which could very well be a one-off) will now yield incorrect velocities instead, and presumably a borked collision response as a result.

Setting everything else before assigning the physics space is something you'll want to do in general anyway, since changing body/shape properties after the body has entered a physics space can potentially be costly, at least with how I've integrated Jolt.

---

So... I've put up a PR (#113712) that only performs the suggested change to `JoltShapedObject3D::get_transform_unscaled`, where we now return the value of the desired/target transform (`kinematic_transform`) if the body is kinematic. I figured this is at least the more intuitive behavior, and fixes issues like `force_update_transform()` not actually updating the transform after moving a kinematic body.

However, while this technically resolves this issue in the sense that you'll see the same stuff printed with both physics engines, you will still (if you don't change the placement of `body_set_space`) end up with the bug that @jrouwe mentioned, where anything potentially overlapping the body at `(0, 0, 0)` will trigger a collision on the first physics step after adding the kinematic body. So please do move that `body_set_space` call instead.

[^1]: I suspect that this is slightly broken in Godot Physics, since it's only the first transform change after we've set the mode to be kinematic, meaning it's not reset when we change physics space.
